Subject: Operational proof and subprocessor routing for no-model-learning commitment

Hi Gwen / Paul —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per Medicorp's procurement/legal asks, attaching a short operational playbook that outlines how Redwood enforces a no-model-learning (no-adapt) commitment for hosted and dedicated deployments. High level asks we want to align on: 

- Confirmation of the specific DPA amendment language you need (we outlined suggested text in the attachment).
- The list of proof points your legal team requires (e.g., KMS residency, SOC2 audit excerpts, subprocessor inventory with transit paths).
- Preferred evidence delivery: secure SFTP vs presigned S3 bundle vs DocuSign/e-sign acknowledgement.

Quick note about subprocessor routing: we can route your traffic to onshore-only GPU pools and SFTP egress where required. We also support an explicit subprocessor transit restriction in the DPA (we provide the operational controls to enforce it).

Attachment: redwood-no-learn-operational-playbook.pdf (4 pages) — includes: enforcement flags in routing layer, ephemeral KV cache configuration, model-variant fallback policy, and subprocessor transit map.

Can you confirm your legal team's top 3 evidence items and whether procurement needs a single consolidated artifact or individual docs? We'd like to get this in front of our Contracts team for a targeted amendment.

Thanks,
Naomi

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear deck.

High level from Legal/Procurement:
1) We need explicit DPA language: no-model-learning (no adaptive training) for Medicorp data, plus an assurance around prompt/response ownership (Medicorp retains ownership; provider must not use outputs to improve models).
2) Evidence requested: SOC 2 (latest report), a completed subprocessor inventory with transit paths, and an ops runbook showing how onshore routing is enforced.
3) Delivery: procurement prefers a secure SFTP upload of the artifacts and a one-page summary we can share with our legal counsel.

Please also include the list of subprocessors and whether any subcontracted vendors have access to raw prompts.

I'll loop in procurement (Paul) on scheduling. Legal may follow up with redlines.

— Gwen

Subject: Re: Operational proof and subprocessor routing for no-model-learning commitment

Gwen — 

Appreciate the checklist. A few concrete operational details to address the evidence asks (quick summary here; see attached ops-evidence-quicksheet.txt for a one-page artifact you can use):

- SOC2: we can provide the latest Type II report under CDA terms.
- Subprocessor inventory: current list attached in the playbook; primary subprocessors are (1) managed Kubernetes provider (control plane only), (2) object storage provider for customer egress (onshore buckets available), (3) monitoring/telemetry vendor (only anonymized metrics). None of our core model training vendors have access to customer prompts for hosted Medicorp tenants when no-model-learning is selected.
- Enforcement mechanics: when a customer elects no-model-learning, requests are marked with an operational flag at the routing layer. Those requests are diverted to inference pools that are configured in "no-adapt" mode — these pools: 
  * disable any telemetry forwarding to model-improvement pipelines,
  * flush KV caches after each session (ephemeral KV), and
  * omit persistent logging of prompt contents (only token-level telemetry kept, per retention policy).
- Subprocessor transit: we support pinned egress lanes. For Medicorp we can pin to onshore SFTP egress or to a dedicated onshore object-store path; subprocessors used for telemetry/metrics are restricted from exporting raw prompts.

Attachments: ops-evidence-quicksheet.txt — bulletized evidence you can upload to procurement.

If legal needs a short technical addendum we can produce a one-page attestation signed by our Head of Ops and CISO. Would that satisfy the evidence requirement?

Thanks,
David Kim
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Gwen Hayes <gwen.hayes@medicorp.com>, Paul Miller <paul.miller@medicorp.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Operational proof and subprocessor routing for no-model-learning commitment

Gwen / Paul —

Thanks for the clear asks. From a contracts perspective we suggest two pragmatic steps to keep procurement moving while legal finalizes redlines: 

1) Proposed DPA amendment snippet (language you can drop into your review):

"Provider shall not use Customer Content (including prompts and responses) to improve, fine-tune, or otherwise train any models or services used to provide the Services to Customer. Provider will ensure that any Subprocessor that receives Customer Content in the course of providing the Services is contractually obligated not to use the Customer Content for model training or model improvement. Customer retains all ownership rights in prompts and generated responses; Provider grants no rights to derivatives for the purpose of model improvement."

2) Evidence path: accept a combined upload to your secure SFTP of (a) SOC2 Type II redacted report, (b) signed one-page attestation from Redwood Ops/CISO, (c) the subprocessor inventory CSV plus a short transit map. We will produce the attestation and the CSV within 48 hours once you confirm the SFTP endpoint.

3) DocuSign: if procurement prefers, we can publish the amendment as a DocuSign envelope (DEAL-4521 appendix) to speed execution.

Attachment: proposed-dpa-amendment.docx (DPA snippet + metadata table).

Let us know the SFTP host/credentials or whether you prefer HubSpot/DocuSign link. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if that speeds it up.

— Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
